items.text: What three baseline requirements does BLE Rule 1 set for anyone seeking admission to practice law in Michigan?
Be 18 or older, possess good moral character, and have completed, before entering law school, at least 60 semester hours or 90 quarter hours toward an undergraduate degree (Rule 1(A)-(C)).
TRAP: Does BLE Rule 1(C) require a finished bachelor's degree before law school?

No. Rule 1(C) requires only 60 semester hours (or 90 quarter hours) completed before entering law school. The bachelor's-degree requirement most applicants meet comes from the ABA law school's own admission standard, not from Rule 1 itself.
Under BLE Rule 2(B), which law schools are automatically 'reputable and qualified'?
A law school approved by the American Bar Association is reputable and qualified. Other schools may ask the Board to approve them as reputable and qualified, a discretionary decision.
An applicant holds a JD from a non-ABA-approved law school. Can they ever sit the Michigan bar exam?

Possibly. Rule 2(B) lets the Board, in its discretion, permit applicants without an ABA-approved JD to take the exam, considering factors like relevant legal education (such as an LLM) and experience. It is a case-by-case petition, not automatic.
When must a Michigan bar exam application be filed for the February and July exams?
By November 1 for the February exam and March 1 for the July exam. Late applications are accepted until December 15 (February exam) or May 15 (July exam).
What must an applicant disclose to the State Bar character and fitness committee under BLE Rule 2(C)?

Any criminal conviction carrying a possible penalty of incarceration in jail or prison that has not been reversed or vacated, and the applicant must comply with the committee's requirements and requests.
What exam must every Michigan bar applicant pass in addition to the UBE, and who administers it?
The Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE), prepared and administered by the National Conference of Bar Examiners (NCBE). The Board sets the passing score (Rule 2(D)).
What is Michigan's minimum passing MPRE score?
BLE Rule 3(A) defines the Michigan bar exam as the UBE. What three components make up the UBE?
The Multistate Bar Examination (MBE), the Multistate Essay Examination (MEE), and two Multistate Performance Test (MPT) items.
How is the total UBE score weighted across its three components?
MBE 50 percent, MEE 30 percent, MPT 20 percent.
How many questions make up the MEE, and how much total testing time do they take?
Six 30-minute questions. NCBE prints 'six 30-minute questions'; the three-hour total is arithmetic from that, not a figure NCBE states. UBE jurisdictions weight the MEE 30 percent.
What is Michigan's minimum passing UBE score?
268 (out of a possible 400).
Why must a person sitting the UBE in Michigan take all components in a single administration?
To earn a portable UBE score transferable to other UBE jurisdictions; Rule 3(C) requires sitting for and taking all components in one administration to keep that portability.
What is the Michigan Law Component under BLE Rule 3a, and who must complete it?

A course on Michigan-specific topics attorneys licensed in Michigan are reasonably expected to know. It is required before admission by UBE exam, by transferred UBE score, or by admission without examination.
How long is a passing Michigan bar exam score valid?
Three years (Rule 4(D)).
How far in advance of the exam must an Application for Reexamination be filed?
At least 60 days before the examination (Rule 4(C)).
Under Rule 4a, how recent must a transferred UBE score be to qualify for admission in Michigan?
It must have been earned on a UBE administered within the 3 years immediately preceding the Michigan exam date the applicant would otherwise have sat for.
Besides a qualifying score, what else must a transferred-UBE-score applicant complete under Rule 4a?
They must have taken the MPRE and earned the Board's required score, and completed the Michigan Law Component.
Rule 5 lets an out-of-state attorney be admitted without taking the exam. Which two other rules must that attorney still independently satisfy?
Rules 1 and 2(B): the 60-credit pre-law rule and the reputable-and-qualified law school requirement both still apply.
Under Rule 5(B)(5), what practice history must an attorney show to be admitted without examination?

After being licensed and for 3 of the 5 years preceding the application: active practice of law as a principal business or occupation, employment as a full-time instructor in a reputable and qualified law school, or active duty in the armed forces as a judge advocate, legal specialist, or legal officer. Rule 5(A) defines full-time as 21 or more hours per week.
An attorney is approved for admission without examination. How long do they have to take the oath before the certificate lapses?
3 years from the date the certificate of admission is issued (Rule 5(E)).
What are the current BLE fees for the UBE exam, an application for reexamination, and admission without examination?
UBE exam $400 (plus $100 for late filing or transfer); reexamination $300; admission without examination $800 plus the NCBE character-report fee.
Under Rule 7, which two requirements can never be waived, even for good cause?
Payment of fees and the administration of the UBE.
When will Michigan begin administering the NextGen UBE, and when is the last legacy-format exam?

NextGen begins with the July 2028 administration, per NCBE's November 4, 2025 announcement. The last legacy UBE administration is February 2028: NCBE's legacy-UBE page lists February 22 to 23, 2028 as the final legacy test date and describes the legacy exam as administered through February 2028. The NextGen press release itself does not state that date.
Which four subjects drop off the MEE pool starting with the July 2026 bar exam?
Conflict of Laws, Family Law, Trusts and Estates, and Secured Transactions.
From July 2026 through February 2028, how are Family Law and Trusts and Estates still tested on the UBE, even though they leave the MEE?
Through the Multistate Performance Test (MPT), on a transitional basis, rather than through MEE essay questions.
TRAP: Is there a standalone 'Insurance Law' subject on the MEE?

No. Insurance concepts are tested inside Contracts (formation, parol evidence, conditions, damages), Torts (negligence), and Evidence (insurance coverage as a policy exclusion), not as their own named MEE subject.
Under the MEE Evidence outline, what is 'Insurance coverage' listed as?

One of the named items under 'Privileges and other policy exclusions,' alongside attorney-client privilege and spousal immunity. Michigan's own rule is MRE 411: evidence that a person was or was not insured against liability is not admissible to prove the person acted negligently or otherwise wrongfully.
Which four Contracts subtopics on the MEE outline map directly onto how an insurance policy is formed, read, and enforced?
Formation of contracts (mutual assent, consideration), parol evidence, conditions (express and constructive), and expectation interest with causation and foreseeability.
What five elements does Michigan recite for a valid contract, and which national shorthand is the trap?

Hess v Cannon Twp, 265 Mich App 582, 592 (2005), quoting Thomas v Leja, 187 Mich App 418, 422 (1991): '(1) parties competent to contract, (2) a proper subject matter, (3) a legal consideration, (4) mutuality of agreement, and (5) mutuality of obligation.' The four-part offer, acceptance, consideration and mutual assent list is bar-outline shorthand, not what a Michigan court recites.
Titan Ins Co v Hyten confirms insurance policies are treated as what for construction purposes?

Ordinary contracts: 'subject to the same contract construction principles that apply to any other species of contract,' absent an applicable statute (quoting Rory v Continental Ins Co, 473 Mich 457 (2005)).
State Michigan's parol evidence rule as quoted in UAW-GM Human Resource Center v KSL Recreation Corp, and say who actually wrote it.

'[P]arol evidence of contract negotiations, or of prior or contemporaneous agreements that contradict or vary the written contract, is not admissible to vary the terms of a contract which is clear and unambiguous.' UAW-GM, 228 Mich App 486 (1998), is quoting Schmude Oil Co v Omar Operating Co, 184 Mich App 574, 580 (1990). UAW-GM's own holding is the merger-clause rule.
When a written contract has a valid merger clause, when can parol evidence still defeat it under UAW-GM v KSL?
Only in cases of fraud that invalidate the integration clause itself, or where the agreement is obviously incomplete 'on its face.'

An adjuster verbally promises a homeowner extra coverage beyond the signed, unambiguous appraisal agreement, which contains a merger clause. Can the homeowner use that phone call to override the writing?

Generally no. Under the parol evidence rule, an unambiguous written contract with a valid merger clause controls over a prior or contemporaneous oral promise that contradicts it, absent fraud attacking the integration clause itself.
What does a silent-fraud (fraudulent concealment) claim require that ordinary actionable fraud does not, and which case does UAW-GM cite for it?

A duty to disclose the concealed fact, rather than an affirmative false statement: 'The false material representation needed to establish fraud may be satisfied by the failure to divulge a fact or facts the defendant has a duty to disclose.' UAW-GM cites McMullen v Joldersma, 174 Mich App 207, 213 (1988) for silent fraud, and cites US Fidelity & Guaranty Co v Black, 412 Mich 99, 116 (1981) for innocent misrepresentation. Do not swap them.
How does Michigan define a condition precedent, and what happens if the party who owes performance is the one who blocks it?

'A fact or event that the parties intend must take place before there is a right to performance.' Harbor Park Market v Gronda, 277 Mich App 126, 131 (2007), quoting Mikonczyk, 238 Mich App 347, 350 (1999). If the condition is not satisfied there is no cause of action for failure to perform. But a promisor who prevents the condition waives it: 'there is an implied agreement that the promisor will place no obstacle in the way of the happening of such event.'
What is the general Michigan rule when an insured misses a policy's sworn proof-of-loss deadline?

'Failure to timely provide a sworn statement in proof of loss within the explicit time requirement contained in the insurance policy is an absolute bar to an insured's recovery,' subject to waiver or estoppel.

An insurer never sent the insured a copy of the policy despite repeated requests and never supplied a proof-of-loss form, then denied for a late proof of loss. What is the insured's defense, and does the insurer have to show it was prejudiced?

Waiver or estoppel: on those facts Dellar held the insured 'was entitled to raise a question of fact before a factfinder whether waiver or estoppel occurred.' Prejudice is irrelevant to the bar itself: 'the failure to file a signed and sworn proof of loss within sixty days of the loss bars recovery on a claim without regard to whether the insurer is prejudiced by such failure.' Dellar v Frankenmuth Mut Ins Co, 173 Mich App 138 (1988).

In Dupree v Auto-Owners Ins Co, 497 Mich 1 (2014), what did the Michigan Supreme Court hold about a policy paying only actual cash value 'until actual repair or replacement of such property is completed'?

The repair-completion language is a condition precedent, so an appraisal award does not turn withheld depreciation into a judgment: 'plaintiff's failure to submit proof of actual loss in accordance with that provision entitles her to only the actual cash value of her damaged personal property.' MCL 500.2826 expressly allows a fire policy to say there is no liability unless the property is actually repaired, rebuilt, or replaced.
State the Hadley v Baxendale rule as adopted by the Michigan Supreme Court in Kewin v Massachusetts Mutual Life Ins Co.
'The damages recoverable for breach of contract are those that arise naturally from the breach or those that were in the contemplation of the parties at the time the contract was made.'
Under Kewin, can a policyholder generally recover mental-distress damages for a wrongfully denied ordinary insurance claim?

No. Applying Hadley v Baxendale to an ordinary commercial contract generally limits damages to the contract's monetary value had it been performed; mental-distress damages are not ordinarily recoverable for breach of an insurance contract.
What narrow exception to Kewin's damages limit comes from Stewart v Rudner, and did Kewin extend it to an ordinary disability policy?

Stewart allows mental-distress damages for contracts 'concerned not with trade and commerce but with life and death... matters of mental concern and solicitude' (there, a promised Caesarean delivery). Kewin declined to extend that exception to an ordinary disability insurance policy.
Does a bad-faith breach of an insurance contract, by itself, state an independent tort claim in Michigan?
No. Kewin held that a bad-faith breach of an insurance contract does not state an independent tort claim absent a duty independent of and apart from the contractual undertaking.
List the six elements of actionable fraud (fraudulent misrepresentation) under Michigan law, per Titan Ins Co v Hyten.

(1) A material representation, (2) that was false, (3) known false or made recklessly, (4) intended to be acted upon, (5) actual reliance, and (6) resulting injury. All six must be proved; the absence of any one is fatal to recovery.
What did Titan Ins Co v Hyten hold about an insurer's fraud defense when the misrepresentation was 'easily ascertainable' and the claimant was an injured third party?

The insurer may still avoid or limit liability for fraud in the application, even where the fraud was easily ascertainable and the claimant is a third party. The Court overruled the 'easily ascertainable' rule from Kurylowicz, and stated the general principle: 'none of these doctrines requires that the party asserting fraud prove that the fraud could not have been discovered through the exercise of reasonable diligence.' There is no duty to investigate.

A driver checked 'no unlicensed or suspended drivers in the household' on an auto policy application while her license was actually suspended. The insurer could have checked the Secretary of State's records. Does the insurer lose its fraud defense?
No. Titan v Hyten rejects the argument that an insurer loses its fraud defense merely because the fraud was easy to check; there is no 'easily ascertainable' exception in Michigan.
What four essential elements does every Michigan negligence action require, per Kandil-Elsayed v F & E Oil, Inc?
Duty, breach, causation, and harm.
How did Kandil-Elsayed (2023) change where Michigan analyzes the open-and-obvious danger doctrine?
It overruled Lugo v Ameritech Corp's treatment of open-and-obvious danger as part of duty. Open-and-obvious risk is now analyzed as part of breach and comparative fault, decided by the jury.
TRAP: A study guide says an open and obvious hazard means the landowner owed no duty at all, citing the 'special aspects' test. Is that still good law?

No. Kandil-Elsayed (2023) overruled that framework. Whether a duty exists is a question of law for the court, but open-and-obvious is now weighed in breach and comparative fault, a jury question, not in duty.
Under Kandil-Elsayed, is 'whether a duty exists' decided by the judge or the jury? What about 'whether the defendant breached that duty'?
Whether a duty exists is a question of law decided by the court; whether the defendant breached that duty is a question of fact for the jury.
What is Michigan's general statute of limitations for an action to recover damages for injury to a person or property, under MCL 600.5805(2)?
3 years after the time of the death or injury.
What is Michigan's statute of limitations for an action charging assault, battery, or false imprisonment, under MCL 600.5805(3)?

2 years. Subsections (4) and (5) set 5 years where the assault or battery was by a spouse, former spouse, a person with whom the plaintiff has a child in common, a current or former household member, or someone in a dating relationship with the plaintiff.
What is Michigan's statute of limitations for a products liability action, under MCL 600.5805(12)?
3 years; for a product in use 10 or more years, the plaintiff must prove the prima facie case without the benefit of any presumption.
What is Michigan's statute of limitations for an action charging libel or slander, under MCL 600.5805(11)?
1 year.
What is Michigan's general statute of limitations for an ordinary breach-of-contract action, under MCL 600.5807(9)?
6 years, for a breach-of-contract action not otherwise described in subsections (2) through (8) of the same section.
TRAP: A homeowner wants to sue on a denied fire-policy claim 3 years after the loss. Does the 6-year general contract SOL (MCL 600.5807(9)) let the suit proceed?

No. The Standard Fire Policy's own 1-year suit clause, MCL 500.2833(1)(q), controls over the general 6-year contract SOL for that specific policy provision; the general rule does not override the insurance code's own specific deadline.
What did the May 1, 2024 amendment to MRE 702 change about expert testimony?

It requires the proponent of an expert's testimony to demonstrate it is more likely than not that the admission factors are satisfied, and clarifies that it is the expert's opinion that must reflect a reliable application of principles and methods to the facts. ADM File No. 2022-30, entered March 27, 2024. The same order amended MRE 804(b)(4)(B). Federal Rule of Evidence 702, amended effective December 1, 2023, now reads the same way, but the Michigan order does not say it was copying it.
What does MRE 411 say about evidence that a person was or was not insured against liability, and what is the exception?

'Evidence that a person was or was not insured against liability is not admissible to prove whether the person acted negligently or otherwise wrongfully. But the court may admit this evidence for another purpose, such as proving a witness's bias or prejudice or if controverted proving agency, ownership, or control.' The bar is on the fault inference only, not on every use of insurance evidence.
An applicant scored 268 on the UBE in another state exactly 3 years and one month before the Michigan exam date they would otherwise sit for. Can they transfer that score under Rule 4a?
No. Rule 4a(A)(2) requires the score be earned on a UBE administered within the 3 years immediately preceding that Michigan exam date; one month past the window disqualifies the transfer.
A licensed out-of-state attorney wants Michigan admission without examination but has only practiced law for 2 of the last 5 years (the rest spent unemployed). Do they qualify under Rule 5(B)(5)?

Not automatically. Rule 5(B)(5) requires 3 of the preceding 5 years in qualifying activity (active practice, full-time teaching, or JAG service), though the Board may extend the 5-year period for good cause.
